SPECIFICATION FOR 

RETRACTOR, MASTOID, SELF-RETAINING 
(MOLLISON’S PATTERN) 


1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for self-retaining mastoid retractor ( Mollison's pattern) 
used in ENT surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 



3. Maierials 

Component 

Material 

Conforming to 

Arms 

Stainless steel 

Designation 22Crl3 or 30Crl3 of Schedule 

Ratchet arrangement 

Stainless steel 

V of IS: 1570-1961 'Schedules for 
wrought steels for general engineering 
purposes’ 

Designation 22Crl3, 30Crl3 or 20Crl8Ni2 

and pivot screw 

Spring 

Stainless steel 

of Schedule V of IS: 1570-1961 
Designation 30Crl3 of Schedule V of IS: 


1570-1961 


4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 All the surfaces, except the ratchet teeth, shall be smooth and free from pits, and the edges shall 
be even.

Alteration 

( Page 2, clause 6.3 ) — Substitute the following for the existing clause: 

"6.3 Corrosion Resistance — The instrument shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test as 
specified in IS : 7531-1975 ' Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of 
stainless steel surgical instruments 


(CPDC 26) 


Printed at Neelkamal Printers, Delhi, India 



IS : 5720 - 1970 


4.2 The edges of the retracting prongs shall taper to a blunt point. 

4.3 The retractor arms shall open and close smoothly without any friction or undue resistance or play at 
the Joint. 

4.4 The ratefiet teeth shall be well cut. clean, uniform, regular and evenly spaced. 

4.5 The ratefiet teeth shell engage accurately and securely and shall effectively lock the retractor at any 
desired position. 

4.8 The ratefiet arm with the finger rest pressed shall swivel freely. The spring shall not be too stiff. 

4.7 The retractor shell be passivated and finished dull. 

5. Heat Treatmentment — The retractor, except the springs, shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness 
6 f 3 80to 400 HV. The spring shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 400 to 460 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Open the arms of the refractor to about 75 mm measured at the tip. Grip the retractor at the retract¬ 
ing blades between the thumb and the forefinger and apply force trying to close the blades. The ratchet 
shall not slip under the force and shall show no sign of damage on removal of the force. Repeat the test 
with 3 different arm openings. 

6.2 Open the arma aa above. Apply a force of 70N (7 kgf approximately) between each oppoaite pair of 
retracting prongs tending to close the retractor. Apply the force gradually and maintain for 2 minutes. 
On completion of the test the retractor shall show no sign of damage. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance — Scrub the retractor with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and then 
dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the retractor. Immerse in copper sulphate aolution at room tempera¬ 
ture for 6 minutes and wash off with fresh water or wet cotton wool. The solution shall be made up 
as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CUSO 4 . 5 H 2 O ) 4.0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( H2SO4 ) (sp gr 1.84 ) 10.0 g 

Water ( H 2 O ) 90.0 ml 

No red stains or spots on the retractor shall be allowed but dulling of the polished surface mey be 
permitted. 

7. Marking —Each retractor shall be marked with the following; 

a) Manufacturer'a name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) The words 'stainless steel’. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available from the Indian Standards institution. New Delhi.’ 

8 . Packing — Each retractor shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or put in a polyethylene bag. 
Each such retractor shall be pacited in an individual cardboard carton. The packing may also be done as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the auppller.
